column3: NKJV reads נִר (“the lamp”) as “the plowing,” a different vowel reading.
Close to the Hebrew; לְמוֹתָר (“to profit”) is rendered “to plenty.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a breath driven about, seekers of death” is rendered “the fleeting fantasy of those who seek death.”
Close to the Hebrew; יְגוֹרֵם (“will sweep them away”) is rendered “will destroy them.”
NKJV renders “the righteous one” as “The righteous God,” supplying “God,” and “to calamity” as “for their wickedness.”
Close to the Hebrew; “in the bosom” is rendered “behind the back.”
Close to the Hebrew; וּמְחִתָּה (“terror, ruin”) is rendered “destruction will come.”
Close to the Hebrew; רְפָאִים (“the shades”) is rendered “the dead.”
Close to the Hebrew; “covenant loyalty” is rendered “mercy.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the strength of its trust” is rendered “the trusted stronghold.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “He” (the lazy man) as subject of “covets.”
Close to the Hebrew; “will speak to perpetuity” is rendered “will speak endlessly,” and NKJV supplies “him.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV follows the traditional reading “establishes his way” (written “considers”).
Close to the Hebrew; “before the LORD” is rendered “against the LORD.”
